newsitem.title: USA: California mother says didn't neglect obese child.
newsitem.headline: California mother says didn't neglect obese child.

text.p: A California woman whose daughter weighed 680 pounds (310 kgs) when she died and was allegedly covered in bed sores, bugs and filth pleaded not guilty on Thursday to a charge of felony child endangerment.

Marlene Corrigan, a 48-year-old federal employee, entered the plea during a short arraignment hearing in a municipal court in Richmond, 20 miles (32 kms) northeast of San Francisco. She declined to talk to reporters outside.
Corrigan's daughter, Christina, 13, died last Nov. 19 at her home in nearby El Cerrito. A medical examiner concluded that she died of congestive heart failure due to obesity.

"The basis of the charge is the condition of the home which the child was in and the condition of her body and the fact that her mother had failed to seek any kind of medical care for those conditions," said Contra Costa County Deputy District Attorney Brian Haynes.
Haynes said that for months at a time before her death, the girl had lived in the nude on the living room floor covered in a sheet.
Haynes said Corrigan told police that she did not know what to do about her daughter and was waiting for a miracle.
The child endangerment charge carries a maximum potential sentence of six years in prison.
